title: Java News Roundup: Grails 8, Open Liberty, GlassFish, Infinispan, LangChain4j, Spock
gist: InfoQ's Oct 5, 2026 Java roundup covers four JEPs moving toward JDK 28 (adaptive ZGC heap sizing, faster ZGC startup, finalizing Structured Concurrency after seven previews, Lazy Constants), plus releases of Apache Grails 8.0, Open Liberty, GlassFish 8.0.5, Infinispan 16.3, LangChain4j 1.22 and others.

insights.claim: JEP 546 (Adaptive Heap Sizing for ZGC) was moved to Proposed to Target for JDK 28; it would let ZGC adjust heap size to available resources, application needs and neighbouring applications competing for the same resources, with review ending October 14, 2026.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Automatic heap sizing in ZGC could cut memory tuning and cloud cost for latency-sensitive Java services sharing hosts; watch the JDK 28 target decision.
insights.quote: enhance the Z Garbage Collector to adaptively adjust the size of the heap based on the resources available, the application's needs, and the needs of neighboring applications contending for the same resources.
insights.locator: JEP 546, Adaptive Heap Sizing for ZGC

insights.claim: JEP 545 (Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC) is Proposed to Target for JDK 28 and aims to have ZGC acquire and prepare physical memory more swiftly in response to application needs, with review ending October 14, 2026.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Faster startup and warmup matters for autoscaled and serverless Java workloads where cold-start cost is billed.
insights.quote: improve application startup and warmup by enhancing the Z Garbage Collector to acquire and prepare physical memory more swiftly and efficiently in response to application needs.
insights.locator: JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC

insights.claim: JEP 543 proposes finalizing Structured Concurrency without change in JDK 28, after seven preview rounds from JDK 21 through JDK 27 and two incubator rounds in JDK 19 and 20; review ends October 13, 2026.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Finalization gives teams a stable API for concurrent code, removing the preview-flag barrier to production adoption.

insights.claim: JEP 547 elevates Lazy Constants to Candidate status for a fourth preview with no changes; the feature, formerly Stable Values and Computed Constants, provides immutable holders initialized at most once, offering final-field performance and safety with flexible initialization timing.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Another preview round signals the API is not yet final, so production use remains premature.

insights.claim: JDK 28 early-access Build 19 was released, containing issue fixes over Build 18.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Shows JDK 28 is progressing through regular early-access builds.

insights.claim: GlassFish 8.0.5 delivers bug fixes, dependency upgrades, ZIP64 extra-field header handling in ZipPayloadImpl, and improved deployment time for both large and small applications.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Maintenance release; relevant mainly to Jakarta EE reference-implementation users.

insights.claim: Apache Grails 8.0.0 requires JDK 21 and Gradle 9.7 as minimum versions, makes all controllers REST resources resolved from the request rather than the mapping, and runs Grails Promises on the Spring Boot Task Executor.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: The JDK 21 floor and controller-resolution change are breaking-upgrade items for Grails shops.

insights.claim: Open Liberty 26.0.0.10 supports JDK 27 and fixes seven CVEs, and with G1 now the default GC in all environments, users in constrained environments may see different garbage-collection behavior than in earlier Java versions.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Teams on small containers should test GC behavior and memory footprint before upgrading.
insights.locator: The GA release of Open Liberty 26.0.0.10

insights.claim: Micronaut Framework 5.2.2 updates to Netty 4.2.19.Final, resolving 16 CVEs including HTTP request/response smuggling and unbounded resource consumption in the HTTP, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 codecs.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Netty-level vulnerabilities propagate to many Java services; prompt patching of HTTP codecs is warranted.

insights.claim: Spock 2.5.0 adds support for Groovy 6 and Spring Framework 7, improves TooManyInvocationsError to report unsatisfied interactions, and allows final local variables in where: blocks.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Signals the Groovy/Spring testing stack tracking the newest major versions.

themes.theme: Data, compute and AI library releases

insights.claim: Infinispan 16.3.0 (codename Tripel Karmeliet) adds more efficient hash-based conflict detection and resolution when merging partitions, configuration attributes persisted across restarts, and reduced log noise.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Partition-merge efficiency improves robustness of distributed caches.

insights.claim: LangChain4j 1.22.0 adds a BedrockBatchChatModel implementing BatchChatModel on the Bedrock batch inference API, and OpenAiDecisionModel and OpenAiOfficialDecisionModel to support the OpenAI Decisions API.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Shows Java LLM tooling adding batch inference and structured decision APIs from major providers.
insights.locator: The formal release (along with the thirty-second beta

insights.claim: TornadoVM 7.2.0 and 7.1.0 add mmaLoadA() and mmaLoadB() to KernelContext returning 8-element and 4-element HalfFloat fragments, and fix CUDA classes to accurately report driver dispatch time for kernel launches and data transfers.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Half-precision matrix-fragment support points to Java GPU acceleration targeting ML-style workloads.
